title: Two independent candidates beat the fixed baseline by 6x and 7x on an arithmetic-bound task, winning every timing pair, but neither is qualified because the measurement failed the stability gate

evidence.note: first attempt, R1024/K128/N64, dispatches_per_sample 64: run_fault at turn 2 event 13, broker error evaluator_failed, failure_class TimeoutExpired, metal-observer exceeded its 300s default. The paired protocol issues roughly 10 pairs x 2 arms x 25 samples x 64 dispatches, and at that shape each program loads the whole 128x64 operand, so the shape was too large for the timeout rather than the harness being at fault. No evaluation completed and 333,169 provider tokens were spent

second attempt, R256/K64/N64, dispatches_per_sample 8, 2 turns: protocol_adherence adhered, three search and three attribution evaluations completed, terminal no_qualified_candidate at provider_token_limit with 554,714 tokens. Candidate b57e32f9 pooled medians baseline 1.2141ms candidate 0.1676ms speedup 7.24 with pair_wins candidate 10 baseline 0; candidate 67d659f2 baseline 1.2108ms candidate 0.2017ms speedup 6.00 with pair_wins candidate 10 baseline 0. Both carry classification measurement_quality_failed

observation: On the arithmetic-bound gemm task two independently authored candidates each beat the fixed baseline by a wide margin -- 7.24x and 6.00x on pooled medians -- and each won all ten timing pairs against it, where the protocol requires six. Correctness was clean for both arms on all five declared input cases in preflight and postflight and on ten timed output checks, with worst absolute error 7.63e-06 for the candidate and 9.54e-06 for the baseline against a contract allowance of 1.07e-04. Neither candidate qualified. Both were classified measurement_quality_failed: over 280 per-dispatch samples the candidate's coefficient of variation was 0.467 and the baseline's 0.133 against a limit of 0.05, and relative IQR was 0.164 and 0.145 against the same limit. The distribution is not broadly noisy -- 66% of samples on each arm sit within 5% of their median and the minima are tight -- it is a clean mode with a heavy upper tail reaching six times the median. Two conditions plausibly produce that tail and both were present: dispatches_per_sample was set to 8 rather than the default 64, which amortizes fixed command overhead eight times less per timed buffer, and the timing record states external_gpu_activity not_excluded, so other work on the device was not fenced off. The separation from F-2026-09-10-004 is the point worth keeping. That finding now spans ten completed campaigns across five workload families -- affine normalization, backward, reduction, gated activation and in-place optimizer update -- and not one candidate in any of them reached the 1.05 materiality ratio, with per_channel_moments evaluating twelve candidates without approaching it. Every one of those ten tasks is bandwidth-bound: measured with the Compiler's work model they span 0.20 to 1.50 counted FLOPs per compulsory byte, and the one contraction among them, the legacy gemm_bias, was frozen at N=16 which caps it at 6.7. Here the first arithmetic-bound task at 14.2 produced a 600% gap on the first completed campaign, with both candidates winning every pair. The ceiling F-004 reports is consistent with a property of the task shapes rather than of the provider, and this is the first evidence separating those two explanations -- though an unstable measurement is not yet proof of either.
proposed_change: Do not read this as a qualified speedup: the gate refused it and the gate is right to refuse a measurement with this much spread. Re-run the same shape with dispatches_per_sample at its default 64, which the timing arithmetic now shows fits comfortably -- the observed per-dispatch medians of 1.21ms and 0.17ms put a full 32,000-dispatch protocol at roughly 22 seconds against the 300s observer timeout, where the first attempt's shape did not fit. If the spread persists at the default, the next suspect is external_gpu_activity rather than the protocol. Separately, the first attempt shows that a frozen shape can be large enough to exceed the observer timeout while still lowering and passing every static gate, so shape selection for an arithmetic-bound task needs the dispatch budget checked against the paired protocol before a campaign is launched, not after.
verification_plan: Capability observation, so verification is by campaign rather than replay: re-run gemm at R256/K64/N64 on this Executor with dispatches_per_sample 64 and compare candidate-minus-baseline against the frozen baseline bundle. The claim to be verified is narrow -- that a candidate reaches the 1.05 materiality ratio with at least six pair wins under a measurement that passes the stability gate. Until that run exists this finding records an uncertified gap, not a speedup.
